title: Quell cyclical batcher imbalance causing cross-tenant KV handoff leaks and long-context tail incidents
creator: Rafael Gomez
description: Multiple customer escalations across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments observed intermittent long-context tail latency. Investigation shows a cyclical imbalance in the continuous batching scheduler that occasionally forces KV cache handoffs between worker shards and leaves transient handoff state ("leak") that starves short/medium requests. This ticket tracks the investigation, root-cause, fixes, and controlled rollout.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Run mixed-length workload with >30% long-context (>16k tokens) requests and small conversational bursts (<=64 tokens) on a Dedicated pool.
2) Enable continuous batching with default admission windows and prefetch enabled.
3) Monitor request quantiles and per-tenant KV handoff counters for 1-3 hours.
4) Observe: elevated P95/P99 tail for short requests, repeated KV handoff increments without corresponding completion for several minutes.
investigation_notes: 2025-02-10: Customer A (SaaS analytics) reported sudden P99 jumps after scheduled traffic spike — initial triage pointed to KV eviction storms.
2025-02-11: Reproduced on staging with Dedicated nodes using synthetic mixed-length generator. Found handoff_count++ without handoff_complete under specific admission window oscillations.
2025-02-12: Private deployment (on-prem) upgrade window surfaced similar behavior under maintenance-induced timer drift; indicates bug not limited to cloud metadata services.
2025-02-13: Traced to cyclical admission window shrink/grow loop combined with shard-prefetch rendezvous that can skip cleanup on preemption paths.

2025-02-14: Added extra instrumentation: handoff_id, origin_shard, dest_shard, handoff_state machine transitions. Confirmed stale handoff_state 'PENDING_TRANSFER' persists after dest shard crashes or is preempted.
root_cause: Race between the admission window resizer and the handoff finalizer: when admission window contracts rapidly (microburst reduction) the batcher preempts inflight long-context batches and kicks off KV handoffs. Under a rare scheduling interleaving the destination shard does not ACK handoff completion and the origin shard does not roll back, leaving resources and admission credits in a limbo state that suppresses short-request admission. This is exacerbated by bursty prefetch and timer drift during maintenance windows.
proposed_fixes: 1) Fix handoff finalizer to be idempotent and add a deterministic timeout+rollback path when handoff completion is not observed within 5s.
2) Introduce soft admission credits reserved for short flows (<=128 tokens) that cannot be consumed by pending handoffs — prevents starvation.
3) Harden preemption path: ensure dest shard checkpoint persists handoff acceptance before origin releases KV ownership.
4) Add jittered admission-window resize backoff to avoid tight oscillations during microbursts and maintenance spikes.
5) Add chaos test in CI that simulates shard preemption and network stalls to catch regressions.
rollout_plan: Canary rollout in three phases: (A) internal canary on staging with synthetic mixed-length load (2 hosts) — validate handoff counters and tail latency (48h); (B) Hosted beta region with low-traffic customers and feature-flag enabled routing (72h); (C) Dedicated rollout to small customer clusters with manual monitoring (7 days); Private customers: provide patch and coordination for on-prem upgrade windows. Rollback: feature-flag off + revert handoff timeout to predeploy value.
monitoring_and_alerts: Added new alerts: kv_handoff_pending_ratio > 0.02 for 5m, shortflow_admission_drop_rate > 0.01 for 10m, and batcher_loop_tick_drift > 200ms. Dashboards: per-tenant handoff heatmap and admission-credit utilization. Runbook: page oncall if P95 short-request latency > 300ms above baseline for >10 minutes.
qa_and_acceptance: Automated unit tests for handoff finalizer idempotency.
Integration test: simulated shard preemption with deterministic timing seeds - assert no admission credit leaks.
Performance test: under mixed workload, short-request P99 must be within 1.2x baseline and no sustained KV handoff pending spikes.
Conformance: verify private upgrade path (air-gapped) with offline artifact and DB migration-free patching.
